title: Shipboard Girl
lede: Roy Lichtenstein’s offset lithograph of a smiling blonde woman at a ship’s rail, in red, blue, and yellow dots and flat color with black key lines.
summary: A close-up face in red dots, yellow hair, blue dot sky, and a solid blue block. Roy Lichtenstein, offset lithograph, 1965.

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the V&A image of its copy, CIRC.649-1967 (1400 × 1810 px), in a scratchpad. No image is stored.

styles.note: A clear example of the full process palette: red and blue dot fields, flat yellow and blue, and heavy black outlines on white paper.

context: The V&A records an offset lithograph on paper, sheet 69 × 51.5 cm, printed by Graphic Industries, Inc. and published by Leo Castelli, New York, 1965, signed “R Lichtenstein”. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O1034308/).
observed: The face and neck are covered in red dots on white; the hair is flat yellow with thick black strands.
Two blue dot fields fill the sky at the top and the area behind the shoulder.
A solid ultramarine block with white horizontal stripes sits at lower right.
The lips are flat red with a white highlight shape and a black outline.
A ship’s rail and a rope net are drawn in thick black lines over white.
The image is printed with a wide white margin. There are no speech balloons or words in the image.
interpretation: This print shows the balance of the idiom: roughly equal areas of dot tint, flat color, and white, held together by black.
The dots are large enough to see as dots at print size, which is the scale the style record asks for on screen.
borrow: Use red dots for a warm tint and blue dots for a cool tint, and never mix them in one shape.
Leave generous white around a dense panel so that the dots do not fill the whole page.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The work is © Estate of Roy Lichtenstein.
